messages.subject: Re: Comment on revision r386 in renjin

Comment by mhsatman:

Score: Positive

General Comment:
Implementing the multithreading support would not be easy. The original
interpreter is not thread safe, say that, behaviour of a called function
might not be predicted when it is called by more than one threads, even it
is implemented in Java.

For instance, in statistics classes and random number generators, there
were too many static class elements which are changed while the process is
alive. Basically, I imagine the case that a method is trying the get two
random number from a F distribution. At the same time, another one is
trying to get some random numbers from a standard normal... Those functions
will both use the uniform random number generator functions which are
running as a "finite state machine".

messages.subject: Re: Comment on revision r386 in renjin
parts:
Comment by al...@bedatadriven.com:

General Comment:
Your right, but I think that Renjin's design makes it easy to refactor this
into a thread safe design: the random number generator needs to be
encapsulated into a singleton which is held in the Context.Globals object,
and then mark its generator function as "synchronized".

As long as we've got good test coverage of the existing code, refactoring
can be fun :-)

messages.author: dba36e8d360488ed
messages.subject: Re: Comment on revision r386 in renjin
parts:
Comment by al...@bedatadriven.com:

General Comment:
Actually, now that I think about this, even if we break up the generation
of 7 million random normal variates into 4 worker threads, if our random
number generator is synchronized, it would still have to do all 7 million
in sequence.

What we would really need would be one random generator per thread, right?
But then we wouldn't want them all to use the same seed, so we would have
to figure out what to do when someone calls set.seed() ...

Still, I think there's many primitives that could be easily rewritten to be
multithread, particularly with the new fork/join library that is part of
Java 7 (and is available as library for Java 6), such as sorting or
transposing matrices.

And for all the methods that are marked with @Recycle, we can generate this
code actually....!

General Comment:
it will be problematic even we let the rng as is if at least one
functionalty is multithreaded. I think the permanent solution is to drop
static fields out from the classes and reimplement them in a nonstatic way.

However, this would not the efficient solution since each single thread has
its own rng. A rng distributer/manager class is required for allocating and
deleting rngs, which would be problematic too.

I think the main performance measure should be aabut creating and
manipulating huge matrices, determinants, inverses etc. and leave the
rngs single threaded because they are called at the user level not at the
renjin level.

For example creating a random matrix would be slow but creating it with
static numbers done by a multithreaded way...

It is kinda brain storm, i dont sure about what i say...
